Walt Disney: An American Original is a 1976 non-fictional book by Bob Thomas .

Reception

[ edit ]
Animation historian Didier Ghez considered the book to be the definitive biography of Walt Disney . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ]

Publication history

[ edit ]
The book was later republished by Disney Editions in 1994 and in 2023. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ] [ 7 ]

See also

[ edit ]
* Walt: The Man Behind the Myth - 2001 documentary about Walt
* Golden Age of American animation
* The Disney Version - the 1968 book by film critic Richard Schickel

Walt Disney is an American hero. From Mickey Mouse to Disneyland, he changed the face of American culture. His is a success story like no other: a man who developed animated film into an art form and made a massive contribution to the folklore of the world. After years of research, respected Hollywood biographer Bob Thomas produced a definitive biography of the man behind the legend of Disney: the unschooled cartoonist from Kansas City who when bankrupt on his first movie venture and developed into the genius who produced unmatched works of animation, and ultimately was the creative spirit of an international entertainment empire that has enchanted generations. Complete with a collection of rare photographs, Walt Disney: An American Original is a fascinating and inspirational work that captures the spirit of Walt Disney.

url_citation.title: Walt Disney: An American Original – Some Suggestions for Further Reading – The Imagineering Toolbox
url_citation.content:
Posted on July 25, 2023 Categories Imagineering Library , Walt
I recently read the new Commemorative Edition of Bob Thomas’ WALT DISNEY: AN AMERCIAN ORIGINAL . Though I’ve read dozens and dozens of books about Disney parks and about Walt Disney over the years, and I owned a previous edition of this, I hadn’t read this until this new edition came out. I’m very glad I did. I understand why this is considered the definitive biography of Walt Disney. It’s engaging and meticulously researched, and should be in the library of every Walt Disney fan.

...

When I got to the end of Thomas’ book, I was thrilled to see that the new Commemorative Edition also has an Endnotes section with excerpts from other books about Walt Disney and the Disney company that offer interesting follow up and expansion on some of the events and notes in the book. It seemed that the folks putting together this new edition had thoughts similar to mine in terms of other books that go deeper into some of the subjects that Thomas didn’t have the time or space to explore more thoroughly.

...

So then I had another idea. I could start with a simple list of some suggestions of books for further reading based on the timeline breakdown in Thomas’ book and post it here on

...

The headings that follow correspond to the major sections in Thomas’ book. Within each of those sections I list a few books related to that period of Walt’s life.

The Midwest Years 1901-1923
